skill.name: playwright-best-practices
skill.description: Review Playwright TypeScript tests for stable selectors, assertions, fixtures, parallel execution, and API mocking practices.
skill.summary: Audit Playwright TypeScript tests against practical stability, locator, assertion, and organization guidance.
skill.author: vitalics

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, including example URLs, template literals, relative imports, CI flags, and Playwright API mocks. One real issue remains: SKILL.md requires fetching mutable remote guidelines and treating them as instructions, which can change outside the audited package.

remediation.suggestion: Bundle the reviewed AGENTS.md content in the skill, or pin the source URL to an immutable commit hash.
If remote refresh remains, treat fetched text as untrusted reference material and require user confirmation before applying it.

semantic_findings.title: Mutable Remote Instructions Fetched at Runtime
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md tells the agent to fetch fresh guidelines before each review and then use the fetched content as rules. Because the URL follows a mutable branch, the reviewed package can later execute changed instructions outside this audit.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file explicitly requires WebFetch of latest rules from a branch and says the fetched content contains output instructions. This is a clear supply-chain and prompt-injection surface even though no malicious remote content is present locally.

content.value_statement: Flaky Playwright tests slow releases and reduce trust in automation. This skill reviews tests against focused TypeScript best practices and suggests concrete fixes.
actual_capabilities: Reviews Playwright TypeScript tests against documented best practices.
Flags manual waits, brittle locators, weak assertions, shared state, and poor fixture structure.
Recommends role locators, web-first assertions, page objects, custom fixtures, and test steps.
Covers parallel execution, sharding, test isolation, and API mocking guidance.
Produces concise findings with file and line references when code is provided.
limitations: Requires access to the test files or file patterns supplied by the user.
Guidance targets Playwright with TypeScript and may not fit other frameworks.
It reviews code quality and stability; it does not execute tests by itself.
The current skill fetches guidelines from a remote URL unless revised.

use_cases.title: Stabilize Flaky Test Suites
use_cases.description: Find manual waits, race-prone assertions, and shared test state before they fail in continuous integration.

use_cases.title: Review Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Check new Playwright tests for readable locators, clear assertions, and maintainable page object usage.

use_cases.title: Standardize Automation Patterns
use_cases.description: Apply consistent fixture, sharding, isolation, and API mocking practices across a larger test suite.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Test Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Playwright test file for best practice issues: <file path>.

prompt_templates.title: Locator And Assertion Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review for stability and accessibility.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check <file path> for brittle locators, weak assertions, and missing web-first assertions.

prompt_templates.title: Fixture Refactor Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of setup and teardown design.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the Playwright fixtures in <folder> and suggest changes for isolation, reuse, and cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Suite Architecture Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit <test folder> for page objects, parallel execution, sharding readiness, API mocking, and long-term maintainability.

output: tests/login.spec.ts:18 uses a fixed delay. Replace it with an action or assertion that auto-waits.
tests/login.spec.ts:31 checks text after reading it once. Use a web-first text assertion instead.
tests/cart.spec.ts:12 uses a structural selector. Prefer a role locator with the visible button name.
tests/cart.spec.ts:44 depends on item order. Scope the locator to the cart row before clicking.
tests/fixtures/users.ts:9 creates shared state across workers. Generate isolated users for each test.
tests/fixtures/users.ts:26 lacks teardown. Delete created records after each test fixture completes.

best_practices: Provide the exact test files or folders that need review.
Ask for findings with file and line references for easier triage.
Apply recommendations with small changes, then rerun the affected tests.
anti_patterns: Requesting a broad review without sharing test files or paths.
Using the skill as a substitute for running Playwright tests.
Ignoring accessibility names when adopting role-based locator advice.

faq.question: What test framework does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Playwright tests written in TypeScript.

faq.question: Can it rewrite my tests automatically?
faq.answer: It can suggest changes, but edits depend on the agent and user request.

faq.question: Does it execute Playwright tests?
faq.answer: No. It reviews source files and guidance, but it does not run browsers by itself.

faq.question: What issues can it find?
faq.answer: It can find manual waits, brittle locators, weak assertions, poor fixture design, and parallel execution risks.

faq.question: Does it support JavaScript tests?
faq.answer: Some advice may apply, but the documented examples and type guidance focus on TypeScript.

faq.question: Is remote guideline fetching required?
faq.answer: The current skill requests it. For safer publishing, the author should bundle or pin the reviewed guidelines.
